_: #228 — strings that are user-facing AND must stay one language.
The ledger beside this file counts what is left to translate, and its
target is zero. That target is unreachable while it also counts strings
translating would BREAK, so those are recorded here with the reason, once,
instead of being rediscovered by whoever works the backlog next. An audit
pass already spent two of its findings answering 'leave it'.
An entry is not a way to make a warning go away. Every literal listed here
must still be found in that file by the scanner: an exemption matching
nothing FAILS, so this list cannot outlive the code it excuses. And every
entry needs a `why` somebody can disagree with.

com/loonext/android/core/net/ApiClient.k.why: ApiException keeps a stable English message for crash and support diagnostics, while the adjacent messageKey and messageVars are what customer surfaces render. Translating these diagnostic fallbacks would fragment searchable incidents by device locale; omitting the keys would expose English, so both are enforced here.

Translating it would make incident diagnostics locale-dependent without changing customer UI.

com/loonext/android/features/contacts/de.why: This is an Android ContactsProvider SQL sort clause appended to a column name, not prose. Translating COLLATE NOCASE ASC would change or break query semantics rather than localise a label.

com/loonext/android/features/contacts/Mu.why: These English values are retained solely as stable ApiException diagnostics; both throws carry catalogue message keys that all customer surfaces resolve in the reader's locale. Translating the diagnostic field would make support evidence locale-dependent without translating any UI.

com/loonext/android/features/diagnostics.why: These values belong to the support artifact produced by the developer-only Diagnostics screen, not to its rendered controls (which already use the EN/fr-CA catalogue). The share subjects and export header deliberately stay stable so reports can be searched together, the empty-log sentence is export content sent to that same support channel, and the SimpleDateFormat pattern is executable formatting syntax whose quoted word cannot safely be handed to translation.

com/loonext/android/MainActivity.kt.why: The ViewModel factory string is a private crash invariant that cannot be rendered. The crash-report subject is the stable label attached to an English stack trace sent into the support inbox; the visible dialog, body, button and chooser label all use catalogue copy. Translating either literal would change only incident evidence, not customer UI.

com/loonext/android/ui/common/ImeContrac.why: Debug guard failure assembled for CallFlowLog and error() when a developer breaks the keyboard-avoidance host contract. It deliberately names source concepts and pixel values for diagnosis; translating its fragments would make a crash assertion harder to search without localising any UI.

com/loonext/android/core/model/Countries.why: The country list writes into a freeform address column — the string IS the stored value, not a label over it. Translated, the same workspace stores 'United Arab Emirates' for a member reading English and 'Émirats arabes unis' for one reading French, so two contacts at the same address stop matching and any grouping by country splits in half. The list is one language for the same reason a phone number is one format. Only the multi-word names appear here; the scanner reads them as sentences.

Core/Diagnostics/DiagnosticsReport.swift.why: This is the stable header of the support artifact exported from the developer diagnostics surface, not one of that surface's rendered controls. Translating it would vary incident evidence by device locale without localising UI.

Core/JSONValue.swift.why: This is a private programmer-error invariant emitted only when a value cannot be represented by the JSON model. It is diagnostic vocabulary, not customer copy, and keeping it stable makes failures searchable.

Core/Model/Countries.swift.why: Twin of the Android list, and exempt for the same reason: the string is the stored value of a freeform address column rather than a label over it, so translating it makes the same address store differently depending on who typed it.

Features/Contacts/ContactDetailView.swif.why: This sentence is fixture content inside an Xcode preview, not a shipped label or default shown to a customer. Translating it would only change the developer's representative sample data.

Features/Settings/SettingsRepository.swi.why: This is an HTTP multipart Content-Disposition header prefix. Its exact spelling and escaping are executable protocol bytes consumed by the server, so translating it would corrupt the request rather than localise UI.

app/manifest.ts.why: This is install metadata for the one stable /manifest.webmanifest identity and /inbox start URL, not page copy; the metadata route has no reader locale and a translated value would replace the English installed-app description globally rather than localize a URL-specific surface.

app/(app)/error.tsx.why: Console-only boundary label paired with the Error object for developers and Sentry correlation; the reader sees the translated appShell.segmentErrorTitle and appShell.segmentErrorBody instead. app/error.tsx.why: Both strings are console diagnostics: one reports that best-effort Sentry capture itself failed and one labels the root-boundary Error object. The rendered boundary already uses catalogue keys, so translating these would change only developer incident output.

app/global-error.tsx.why: Console-only label emitted beside the Error object before the boundary renders its catalogue copy. It is incident vocabulary for developers, not a sentence exposed to the reader, so translating it changes diagnostics without localising a surface.

components/auth/turnstile.tsx.why: Private rejected-Promise detail that is deliberately swallowed; the catch sets failed and the person sees onboarding.securityCheckFailed from the catalogue. lib/analytics/posthog.ts.why: Console-only observability bootstrap diagnostic; initialization fails closed to null and no reader sees this label. Translating it would change the developer console and nothing in the product UI.

lib/observability/sentry.ts.why: Console-only observability bootstrap diagnostic emitted when the reporting tool itself cannot start. No UI renders it, and translating it would make incident output vary with a member's language rather than localising customer copy.

lib/push/register.ts.why: The unsupported-browser Error is converted to the translated misc.pushTurnOnFailed fallback, and the registration label is console-only best-effort boot output.
